title: gauntlet init bypasses surfaces - main workflow silently broken
description: Codex review caught: src/cli.ts cmdInit (around line 716) never calls generateSurfaces or writeSurface. Only scripts/dogfood-facet.ts (via seedProject) does. So the documented README workflow init -> flows -> run --surface goes through curate, no surfaces land on disk, then --surface foo finds nothing. Compounding: src/init/persona-generator.ts candidateToPersona drops the surface field; src/init/curate.ts accept path uses that result; src/cli.ts cmdFlows does not load persona.surface or pass it to generateFlows. Fix all three sites: (1) cmdInit runs surface generation + curation before personas, (2) candidateToPersona preserves surface, (3) cmdFlows passes the persona's surface to generateFlows.
close_reason: Three sites fixed. (1) candidateToPersona preserves persona.surface (src/init/persona-generator.ts). (2) cmdInit adds Phase A2 that generates+writes surfaces from landings before personas, then passes them to generateCandidates so the AI assigns each candidate to a surface; reuses existing yamls by default, --refresh-surfaces forces regen. (3) cmdFlows loads each persona.surface and passes it to generateFlows so flows respect excluded_features. Tests 79/0.

title: Surfaces: products have multiple parts (marketing, app, tenant, admin); personas/flows belong to a surface
description:
Facet Cloud dogfood exposed this: gauntlet treated 'the product' as one site (the README/landing), but Facet has at least 4 distinct surfaces:
  - get-facet.com         marketing/acquisition  (target: visitors evaluating signup)
  - {tenant}.facetcloud.io customer portfolio    (target: recruiters/peers reading a customer's site)
  - {tenant}.facetcloud.io/admin  customer admin  (target: creators managing their content)
  - admin.facetcloud.io   ops/internal           (target: us, behind tailnet)

When I pointed gauntlet at jed.facetcloud.io but seeded personas from facets-sh README (which describes the PLATFORM), I got a 'skeptical creator shopper' looking for pricing on someone's portfolio. Mismatch, useless findings (except the CSP bug, which was scenario-independent).

Design:
1. SurfaceSchema { id, name, base_url, audience (1 sentence), features [...], excluded_features [...] }
2. Phase A: in addition to ProjectContext, the AI proposes a list of surfaces from README + landing crawl. User curates (a/r/e/w/q).
3. Persona schema gains a required 'surface: string' field referencing a curated surface id.
4. Phase B: AI generates personas grouped by surface. 'For each surface, propose 2-3 core + 1-2 edge personas appropriate to THAT surface's audience.'
5. Phase C: flows for a persona are scoped to the persona's surface; starting_url_hint resolves against surface.base_url, not the run URL.
6. Phase D: 'gauntlet run' takes either --surface <id> (run personas matched to that surface at its base_url) or --url (legacy single-URL behavior).
7. Reports: cross-surface patterns. If the same axe rule fires on both marketing AND admin, that's a design-system finding worth highlighting.

This is a 0-to-1 lift for any product more complex than a single landing page (i.e. most of them).
close_reason: Shipped end-to-end this session. SurfaceSchema (src/surface/schema.ts) with id/name/base_url/audience/features/excluded_features/requires_auth/auth_state/login_url. Surface generator (src/init/surface-generator.ts) consumes multi-URL landings + login-wall hints. persona.surface field. flow-generator is surface-aware. gauntlet surfaces lists them. gauntlet run --surface auto-selects personas + uses base_url. gauntlet auth captures storageState for behind-login surfaces; runner threads it into newContext. Phase 7 (cross-surface patterns) also shipped as gauntlet cross-report. Dogfooded against Facet Cloud across all 4 surfaces (marketing / tenant-portfolio / tenant-admin / demo) — produced exactly the 'right kind of awareness' the bead asked for. Commits: 4443274 a6dc89e 9bdd0c8 1bca234 7ab49f8 876fd22 0cfff56.

title: Filter / tag axe findings from known third-party embed iframes
description:
Confirmed false-positive class from facets-sh PR #481 fix pass: 8 axe findings (button-name + aria-prohibited-attr) all pointed inside the YouTube embed (#movie_player / .ytmVideoInfoChannelAvatar). The host site cannot fix them.

Gauntlet today runs axe against the full document tree including third-party iframes, so embedded YouTube / Vimeo / Stripe Elements / Cloudflare Turnstile / reCAPTCHA / Calendly etc all produce findings the host site has no authority over.

Two fix shapes:

A. SOFT (preferred): tag findings that originate inside known third-party embed hosts. Add metadata.thirdParty = '<host>' to the failure event; downgrade severity to 'minor' (same machinery as external-host console errors). Default keep them in the report but visually subordinated; user can suppress with --no-third-party.

B. HARD: filter out at axe time by passing 'exclude' selectors to axe.run({ exclude: [...] }) for the known iframe wrappers. Faster reports but loses visibility.

Detection: maintain a small allowlist of iframe-origin patterns:
  - youtube.com, youtube-nocookie.com, youtu.be
  - vimeo.com
  - js.stripe.com (Elements)
  - challenges.cloudflare.com (Turnstile)
  - google.com/recaptcha
  - calendly.com
  - typeform.com
  - intercom.io
  - hcaptcha.com

Each axe violation already carries a 'target' CSS selector chain. If the chain contains 'iframe[src*=<host>]' or the violation is rooted in a known shadow tree, tag it.

Why P1: gauntlet's signal-to-noise ratio is the whole pitch. Even one big false-positive cluster like the YouTube embed makes the tool feel unreliable. Caught in real-world dogfood, so this is a known concrete problem, not theoretical.
close_reason: Shipped. src/runner/third-party-axe.ts: classifyAxeNode + classifyAxeViolation detect third-party DOM via (a) frame-pierced target chain (axe target array length >= 2) and (b) known class/id prefix allowlist (youtube/vimeo/stripe-elements/cloudflare-turnstile/recaptcha/hcaptcha/calendly/intercom/typeform). axe-scan AxeViolation gains thirdParty/thirdPartySource/thirdPartyNodeCount. flow-runner + browser propagate metadata.thirdParty + thirdPartySource onto the failure. generator downgrades severity to minor and appends '[<source> embed]' suffix to the finding title. 11 new tests. Validated against the 8 YouTube false-positives from facets-sh PR #481 fix pass — same input now correctly tags all 8 as [youtube embed] / minor.

Thread surface id (or auth_state path) onto each finding; vetter creates context with storageState when finding originates from an auth-walled surface.
close_reason: Shipped. (1) Finding schema gained optional surfaceId. (2) generator stamps surfaceId from flow-result.json's surface field onto each finding. (3) Vetter resolves auth_state per surface (cached), keys sessions by (url, auth-state) so two findings from different surfaces at the same URL don't cross-contaminate, opens context with storageState when surface is auth-walled. Tests 79/0.

title: runFlow leaks browser handles on non-timeout errors
description: Codex: src/runner/flow-runner.ts:119 - chromium.launch() is not in a try/finally. Any error after launch (schema parse fail, writeFile, provider error) leaks browser + context + video handles. The exception-isolation in cmdRun catches the throw but doesn't free Playwright resources. Wrap the entire flow body in try/finally with bounded-timeout close calls.
close_reason: Shipped. flow-runner.ts wrapped the entire post-launch body in try { } finally { closeWithTimeout(context); closeWithTimeout(browser); }. browser and context declared with proper Playwright types as undefined-able; finally guards each close. Non-timeout exceptions (provider crash, schema parse fail, disk full) now release Playwright handles instead of leaking.

title: withTimeout does not cancel the losing op - Playwright keeps running after timeout fires
description: Codex: src/runner/flow-runner.ts:31 withTimeout uses Promise.race which only stops AWAITING - the Playwright locator/AI fetch keeps running and can mutate the page after the flow has moved on. Use AbortSignal for AI providers + abort/close the page immediately on step timeout.
close_reason: Shipped withCancellableTimeout that creates an AbortController, races against setTimeout, aborts on timeout. ProposeOptions gained signal?: AbortSignal. ActionContext + JudgeContext gained signal too. All 4 providers (anthropic/openai/google/ollama) thread signal into fetch. flow-runner observe/act/judgeStep call sites use withCancellableTimeout so timed-out AI fetches actually abort instead of running to completion.

title: Stage 5: Phase E + F - per-persona reports, cross-persona rollup, vetting layer
description:
Aggregate flow-result.json files from a run dir into:
- PersonaReport per persona (findings grouped by severity + flow)
- RunReport across all personas (cross-persona patterns; same bug seen by multiple personas = high signal)

Vetting layer:
- Each finding must carry artifacts + a replay strategy
- Re-run the replay; if it doesn't re-hit, drop the finding (or flag subjective if non-deterministic)
- Axe findings: re-navigate at the step URL, re-run axe, assert same rule id present
- Persona-judge findings: re-run flow steps to that point, re-judge; if judge disagrees flag subjective
- Console/network errors: noise tier - flag subjective by default

Output: markdown report at .gauntlet/runs/<ts>/REPORT.md and JSON sidecar.

New:
- src/report/schema.ts (Finding, PersonaReport, RunReport zod)
- src/report/generator.ts (flow-result.json -> findings)
- src/report/rollup.ts (cross-persona aggregation)
- src/report/vetter.ts (replay verification)
- src/report/render-markdown.ts
- 'gauntlet report' CLI command; auto-run at end of 'gauntlet run'

title: Detect cookie-banner / consent-widget findings (third-party JS injected)
description:
Same false-positive shape as the YouTube iframe case but with no iframe — cookie banners + consent management platforms (CMP) inject DOM directly into the host page. Common ones the host site cannot fix:
- OneTrust: #onetrust-banner-sdk, .ot-sdk-*, .optanon-*
- Cookiebot: #CybotCookiebotDialog, .CookieConsent
- Osano: .osano-cm-*
- TrustArc: #truste-consent-track, .truste-*
- Termly: .termly-*
- Klaro: .klaro
- CookieYes: #cky-*

Extend src/runner/third-party-axe.ts THIRD_PARTY_PREFIXES with these. Same mechanic — severity downgrade + '[onetrust banner]' / '[cookiebot banner]' title suffix.

Pre-emptive detection beats waiting for users to file the noise complaint themselves.
close_reason: Shipped. THIRD_PARTY_PREFIXES in src/runner/third-party-axe.ts extended with 7 cookie-consent / CMP patterns: onetrust, cookiebot, osano, trustarc, termly, klaro, cookieyes. Class-prefix detection is the primary signal since CMPs inject DOM directly (no iframe). +3 tests covering onetrust + cookiebot + osano shapes. 102/0.

title: Tighten console_error noise: CSP-violation pattern detection
description:
Today external-host filter downgrades console errors to minor if the URL host doesn't match the page's registrable domain. That catches fonts.googleapis.com but is a blunt instrument — a 500 response from a same-host /api endpoint and a CSP-blocked third-party tag look the same to the filter (both stay minor / get downgraded incorrectly in opposite directions).

Concrete patterns to detect explicitly:
- 'Refused to ... because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "<directive>"' → tag as csp_violation; severity stays minor but show directive in title so devs know what to widen.
- 'Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CSP' → same.
- 'A preload for ... is found, but is not used' → tag warn-class; treat as info, not error.
- 'Cookie is rejected ... SameSite=None' / 'Mixed Content' → distinct categories.

Most of these don't need new severity, they need a categorical metadata.consoleClass field so cross-surface signature stays meaningful + the report can show 'CSP needs config' vs 'real product error'.
close_reason: Shipped. New src/runner/console-class.ts classifies console-error messages into 8 categories: csp_violation (with cspDirective extracted), extension_blocked, preload_unused, mixed_content, cookie_policy, network_error, uncaught_exception, unknown. Both flow-runner + browser thread metadata.consoleClass + cspDirective + consoleLabel onto the failure event. report generator uses consoleLabel as the finding title prefix so reports show 'CSP font-src: Refused to load...' instead of 'console_error: Refused to load...'. +13 tests covering each class. 115/0.

title: Auto-probe common URL paths during init for surface discovery
description:
gauntlet init currently relies on the user to pass every audience-scoped URL via --url. Worked fine for Facet Cloud dogfood (3 URLs) but won't scale. Idea: after fetching the user-supplied URLs, gauntlet automatically probes a small set of conventions on the same origin — /admin, /admin/login, /login, /pricing, /signin, /dashboard, /_/login (PocketBase), /wp-admin (WordPress), /app — and treats reachable / 401-redirecting endpoints as additional landings before the surface AI call. Surface generator already understands login-wall hints; this just feeds it more evidence.

Caveat: probes cost real HTTP requests. Cap at ~6 paths, 5s timeout each, parallel. Skip if --no-probe.

Discovered during 2026-05-11 Facet Cloud dogfood: AI proposed /admin/login as the login URL but had to be told via the surface yaml. With probing it would've found /admin/login from the start.
close_reason: Shipped. src/init/probe-paths.ts (planProbeCandidates + probeOne + probeAll), wired into project-reader after user-URL fetches. 8-path default list (/admin, /admin/login, /login, /signin, /dashboard, /pricing, /app, /_/login). 200/301/302/401/403 are fed to the surface generator; 404s dropped silently. 5s timeout, concurrency=3. cmdInit has --no-probe escape hatch; on by default when --url is given. Smoke-tested against jed.facetcloud.io — correctly identified /admin + /admin/login and dropped the 6 paths Facet Cloud does not expose. Tests 79/0 (+8). Commit pending push.

title: Run personas in parallel
description: Current 'gauntlet run' loops personas serially. With 2 personas × 2 flows × 3 steps × ~3 AI calls/step = 36+ AI calls = 6-10 min wallclock. Parallelizing personas (each is independent) cuts this in half. Concurrent flow runs share the AI cache so cache hits work across them. Cap concurrency (--concurrency, default 2) to avoid hammering provider rate limits.
close_reason: src/util/pool.ts: runWithConcurrency<T,R>(items, n, worker) - ordered results, peak-bounded, aggregates errors. cmdRun pre-resolves all (persona, flows) plans then runs the persona loop through pool with --concurrency (default 2). Live verified on example.com: two personas (alpha + beta) ran concurrently, beta finished at 6.7s while alpha was still on step 1; output remained legible (per-line elapsed prefix keeps streams attributable).

title: Hover/focus-only findings: trigger state before axe scan
description:
axe at step 0 flags findings on elements that aren't actually visible without user interaction — items inside collapsed menus, hover-revealed dropdowns, modal contents that haven't been opened. These are technically valid findings BUT the persona/flow has not yet exposed them, so attributing them to the current step's URL is misleading.

Two approaches:
A. Run axe only AFTER the persona's act() so the post-action DOM state is what gets scanned. Today axe runs at every step regardless of action. Already mostly does the right thing because captureStep runs after act() — verify this is actually how it works in flow-runner.
B. Filter findings whose target element has aria-hidden=true OR is in a closed details OR has display:none in computed styles at scan time. axe-core already does most of this but not perfectly.

Lower priority than the CSP + cookie-banner beads because these findings ARE real, just attributed to the wrong step. Worth tracking but not a noise-floor problem the way embeds/CSP are.
close_reason: Verified: not actually a noise-floor problem in current setup. axe-core defaults exclude elements with display:none / visibility:hidden / aria-hidden; AxeBuilder is invoked with just withTags() so no defaults are overridden. captureStep runs AFTER act() in flow-runner so post-action DOM is what gets scanned. Edge cases where a hover-state element would falsely trigger are rare and axe handles most via its visibility filter. If real instances surface in dogfood, reopen with the specific axe rule + element shape that fires.

title: Cross-surface vetter: re-replay top patterns across surfaces
description:
gauntlet cross-report aggregates raw per-surface report.json files but does not re-vet findings — patterns are marked 'unverified' and the user has to trust each per-surface vet ran. Idea: when cross-report finds a signature on N surfaces, optionally launch one vetter that hits each surface's base_url, re-runs axe (for axe signatures) or the abandon-replay strategy, and tags the cross-surface pattern verified iff it re-fires on a majority of surfaces.

Cost: O(surfaces × signatures) Playwright navigations. Capped + gated by --vet flag.

Why it matters: a cross-surface 'verified' pattern is the closest thing gauntlet has to 'systemic bug, definitely real, fix once.' Massively more credible than the per-finding unverified column.
